exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Foundational horizontal compound press targeting the sternal pectoralis major, anterior deltoids, and triceps.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes directly under the barbell and feet planted firmly.
Retract and depress your scapulae, gripping the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to your lower chest while keeping elbows at ~45-60 degrees.
Drive the bar back up to lockout without losing upper-back tension.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Bench Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
exercises.description: Upper-chest press on a 30-degree incline bench for greater clavicular pec recruitment and shoulder-friendly ROM.
instructions: Set the bench to a 30-degree angle and kick the dumbbells up to shoulder level.
Keep wrists stacked over elbows and lower the dumbbells until you feel a deep stretch across the upper chest.
Press smoothly overhead without clanging the weights together at the top.

media.caption: Watch Incline Dumbbell Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Machine Chest Press
exercises.description: Guided horizontal chest press offering high stability for safely pushing close to muscular failure.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so the handles align with your mid-to-lower chest.
Pin your shoulder blades back into the pad and press the handles forward to full extension.
Control the eccentric for 2-3 seconds without letting the weight stack touch.

media.caption: Watch Seated Machine Chest Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Chest Fly
exercises.description: Constant-tension horizontal adduction isolating the pectoralis major across its full contractile range.
instructions: Set dual pulleys to chest height, grab the handles, and step forward into a staggered stance.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms until a gentle chest stretch is felt.
Sweep your hands together in a wide arc and squeeze your pecs for 1 second at peak contraction.

media.caption: Watch Cable Chest Fly Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the chest, with core, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Lie on an exercise floor mat, face down.
Press your toes against the floor and place your hands flat on the ground shoulder width apart, fingers extended forward.
Descend by flexing at the elbow, lowering your chest toward the ground.
At the bottom contract your chest as you push off the ground and return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the chest, with core, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand resting on top of your thighs.
Press dumbbells straight up into the air and lock arms out at a full extended position and with the dumbbells touching at the peak of the movement.
Return to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Bench Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the chest, with shoulders, triceps assisting.
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench with a dumbbell on each hand resting on top of your thighs.
The palms of your hand will be facing each other.
Lift the dumbbells one at at time.
Hold the dumbbells in front of you, shoulder width apart.
The palms of your hands should be facing each other.
Lift the dumbbells as if you were pressing them stop and hold the weight before you lock out.
Bend your elbows slightly and lower your arms at both sides using a wide arc.
Keep lowering your arms until you feel a stretch on your chest.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Fly Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the chest, with shoulders assisting.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell on each hand and lie on an incline bench that is set to an incline angle of no more than 30 degrees.
Extend your arms above you with your elbows slightly bent.
Rotate your wrists so that the palms of your hands are facing you.
This is the starting position.
Start to slowly lower the arms to the side while keeping the arms extended and while rotating the wrists until the palms of the hand are facing each other.
Exhale and start to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position by reversing the motion.
Rotate your hands so that your pinky fingers are next to each other again.

media.caption: Watch Incline Dumbbell Fly Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the chest, with core, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Lie down on an incline bench.
Gripping the bar with a medium-width grip, lift the bar off the rack.
Hold it straight over your head, keeping your arms locked.
This is the starting position for the exercise.
Remove the bar from the rack, holding the weight above your chest with your arms extended.
Move the bar down toward your upper chest.
Pause for a moment and push the bar back to the starting position.
Arms should be locked.
tags: barbell incline bench press - medium grip

media.caption: Watch Incline Barbell Bench Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Pec Deck (Butterfly)
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the chest.
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad.
Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.
Push the handles together slowly as you squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out during this part of the motion and hold the contraction for a second.
Return back to the starting position slowly as you inhale until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

media.caption: Watch Pec Deck (Butterfly) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Machine Incline Chest Press
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the chest, with triceps assisting.
instructions: Firmly grasp the handles.
Pull your shoulder blades together and lift your elbows to grip level.
Push your arms inclined forward and up till they are fully stretched.
Move the handles towards each other to let your arms meet, then lower them back to your chest at a slightly slower pace.
Repeat the exercise.

media.caption: Watch Machine Incline Chest Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Pull-Up (Bodyweight / Weighted)
exercises.description: Vertical pulling staple for building latissimus dorsi width, teres major, and upper-back thickness.
instructions: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a pronated grip.
Initiate the pull by depressing your scapulae and driving your elbows down toward your hips.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower all the way to a controlled dead hang.

media.caption: Watch Pull-Up (Bodyweight / Weighted) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Cable vertical pull allowing precise load progression for latissimus dorsi and upper back hypertrophy.
instructions: Secure your thighs under the knee pad and grasp the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Lean back slightly (~10-15 degrees) and pull the bar to your upper chest.
Extend your arms slowly overhead until your lats are fully stretched.

media.caption: Watch Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Heavy horizontal compound row developing mid-back thickness, rhomboids, lats, and spinal erectors.
instructions: Hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly 30-45 degrees above parallel with a braced core.
Row the barbell into your lower ribs/upper abdomen while driving elbows behind your torso.
Lower under control without excessive torso heave.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Bent-Over Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: Controlled horizontal cable row targeting the mid-traps, rhomboids, and lats with minimal lower-back fatigue.
instructions: Sit tall with feet braced on the platform and knees slightly bent.
Allow your shoulder blades to protract slightly at the stretch, then row the handle to your midsection.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for 1 second before returning.

media.caption: Watch Seated Cable Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Chin-Up
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the back, with biceps, forearms assisting.
instructions: Facing a pull up bar, grasp the handles with your palms facing away from you and arms at a distance smaller than your shoulder width.
Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down and back.
Exhale during this movement.
Contract your back muscles and then inhale as you extend your arms completely and return back to the starting position.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the back, with biceps, forearms assisting.
instructions: Using a neutral grip, lean into an incline bench.
Grab a dumbbell in each hand and rotate your hands so your palms are facing each other.
Retract the shoulder blades and flex the elbows to row the dumbbells to your side.
Hold for a moment and then lower the dumbbells back down.

media.caption: Watch Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the back, with core, biceps assisting.
instructions: Choose a flat bench and place a dumbbell on each side of it.
Place your right hand and your right knee on the flat bench.
With a straight back and your stomach parallel to the weight bench, grasp the left hand side dumbbell with your left hand, palm facing towards you.
Pull the dumbbell straight up to the side of your chest, keeping your upper arm close to your side and keeping the torso stationary.
Lower the dumbbell until your arm is straight down and your elbow has only a slight bend.

media.caption: Watch One-Arm Dumbbell Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the back.
instructions: Start by grabbing the wide bar from the top pulley of a pulldown machine and using a wider than shoulder-width pronated grip.
Bend your torso slightly forward and keep your elbows slightly bent as you extend your arms straight out in front of you.
Pull the bar down by contracting the lats until your hands are next to the side of the thighs.
Reverse the motion and return to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Straight-Arm Pulldown Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the back, with core, biceps assisting.
instructions: With a dumbbell in each hand, bend your knees slightly and bring your torso forward by bending at the waist; as you bend make sure to keep your back straight until it is almost parallel to the floor.
While keeping the torso stationary, lift the dumbbells to your side (as you breathe out), keeping the elbows close to the body.
On the top contracted position, squeeze the back muscles and hold for a second.
Slowly lower the weight again to the starting position as you inhale.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Bent-Over Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Back Extension
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the back, with glutes, hamstrings assisting.
instructions: Begin by positioning yourself in the back-extension station with legs under leg hooks.
With your body straight, cross your arms in front of you.
Lower body at waist as far down to the ground as comfortably possible.
Make sure to keep back naturally arched, do not bend over too far and curve back.
Slowly raise your torso back to the initial position as you inhale.

media.caption: Watch Back Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the back, with biceps assisting.
instructions: Choose over or under hand grip.
Push chest forward while pulling the bar to your chin.
At the end of the movement, hold your arms tight to your body and accentuate the final position.
Slowly return to initial position and repeat.

media.caption: Watch Close-Grip Lat Pulldown Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Row
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the back, with biceps assisting.
instructions: Sit with your knees slightly bent.
In initial position, your active arm and shoulder are well stretched forward, your body is turned a little to the same side.
Now pull your shoulder and arm all the way back while letting your body turn with the movement.

media.caption: Watch Single-Arm Seated Cable Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Machine Row (Wide)
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the back, with shoulders assisting.
instructions: Sit upright slightly swaying your lower back and keeping good contact to the chest cushion.
Grasp handles at a wide grip, arms stretched and shoulders pushed forward.
Pull handles towards your chest.
Avoid losing contact to the chest cushion.

media.caption: Watch Chest-Supported Machine Row (Wide) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Overhead Barbell Press (OHP)
exercises.description: Strict vertical press building anterior and medial deltoid strength alongside core and triceps stability.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, glutes and abs braced, bar resting on the front delts.
Press the bar vertically past your chin, shifting your head slightly forward once the bar clears.
Lower under control back to the clavicles.

media.caption: Watch Overhead Barbell Press (OHP) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Unilateral-friendly overhead press allowing natural scapular plane movement for deltoid hypertrophy.
instructions: Sit on an upright bench with back support and hold dumbbells at ear level in the scapular plane (~30 degrees forward).
Press overhead to just short of lockout, then lower smoothly to 90 degrees or slightly deeper.

media.caption: Watch Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Essential isolation exercise for the lateral deltoid head to create shoulder width and V-taper.
instructions: Stand tall with a slight forward hip hinge and dumbbells held at your sides.
Raise your arms out in the scapular plane (slightly forward of your torso) until elbows reach shoulder height.
Control the lowering phase without swinging your torso.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Lateral Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Rope Cable Face Pull
exercises.description: Posterior deltoid and external rotator cuff movement critical for shoulder health and posture.
instructions: Set a rope attachment at upper-chest to eye height.
Pull the rope toward your forehead while externally rotating your shoulders so your thumbs point behind you.
Pause briefly at peak contraction before extending your arms.

media.caption: Watch Rope Cable Face Pull Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the shoulders, with biceps, forearms assisting.
instructions: Keep a tight core and flat back as you remain seated in the shoulder press machine.
Look straight ahead as you hold on to the handles.
Slowly, press the handles up above your head.
Do not lock out your elbow.
Slowly, bring the handles back down but do not let the weight stack touch.
Repeat the movement.

media.caption: Watch Machine Shoulder Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders, with biceps, triceps assisting.
instructions: Set up an adjustable angle bench to 90 degrees and grab two dumbbells from the rack.
Pick up the dumbbells from the floor using a neutral grip (palms facing in).
Position the end of the dumbbells on your knees and sit down on the bench.
Using a safe and controlled motion, kick your knees up one at a time in order to get each dumbbell into place.
Once the dumbbells are in place, rotate your palms so they are facing you.
Take a deep breath then press the dumbbells overhead by extending the elbows and contracting the deltoids.
As you press, rotate the dumbbells until your palms are facing forward.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position (the arms should be roughly 90 degrees or slightly lower depending upon limb lengths).

media.caption: Watch Arnold Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders, with triceps assisting.
instructions: Stand upright and keep the back straight.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand at the shoulders with an overhand grip.
Thumbs should be on the inside and knuckles facing up.
Raise the weights above the head in a controlled motion while exhaling.
Pause at the top of the motion.
Return the dumbbells to the shoulders while inhaling.

media.caption: Watch Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Guided isolation exercise for the lateral deltoids with constant tension and no momentum.
instructions: Sit upright in the machine and adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the pivot points, with the pads resting against the outside of your upper arms. This will be your starting position.

Keeping your torso still (no swinging), raise your arms out to the sides with a slight bend in the elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the floor. Exhale as you lift and pause for a second at the top.
Lower the pads slowly back to the starting position as you inhale, without letting the weight stack touch down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

media.caption: Watch Machine Lateral Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: Stand with your side to the machine, arm before your body, grasping the handle by a firm grip.
Lift your arm sideways and up.
Keep your elbow slightly bent during the entire movement.
Change arms.
tags: standing one-arm side lift with cable

media.caption: Watch Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Front Raise
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: Grab a barbell and stand up straight.
Adopt a pronated, shoulder-width grip on the barbell.
Try to keep the torso stationary and lift the barbell to the front until your arms are slightly above the level where they would be parallel to the floor.
Then slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat as necessary.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Front Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: Pick up two dumbbells and stand up straight.
The dumbbells should be positioned in front of your thighs with your hand facing down.
While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the left dumbbell to the front with a slight bend on the elbow and the palms of the hands always facing down.
Continue until you arm is slightly above parallel to the floor.
Lower the left dumbbell down slowly until you reach the starting position.
Lift the right dumbbell up at the same time.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Front Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Upright Row
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the shoulders, with back assisting.
instructions: Set the handle of the cable machine to the lowest notch.
Grasp the bar with both hands and palms facing down.
Bending at the elbows pull the bar up to the top of your chest.
Lower the bar back to you waist.

media.caption: Watch Cable Upright Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Fly
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: Lie down on an incline bench with the chest and stomach pressing against the incline.
Have the dumbbells in each hand with the palms facing each other.
Place your arms extended straight out and slightly downward, palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent.
Place your feet slightly wider than shoulder width apart and ground your toes for your starting position.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades, until your arms are parallel to the floor and the dummbells are shoulder high.
Feel the contraction and slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Reverse Fly Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: Sit with your chest against the cushion, arms between the cushions.
Push your arms sidewards so that your shoulder blades are pulled together.

media.caption: Watch Reverse Pec Deck Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Fly
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the shoulders, with back assisting.
instructions: Stand with your arms crossed before your hips, firmly grasping the handles.
Lift your arms sideways and up, elbows slightly bent during the entire movement.
Slowly lower again and repeat.

media.caption: Watch Cable Reverse Fly Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the shoulders, with back assisting.
instructions: Stand behind a barbell with your feet shoulder width apart.
Raise your shoulders up as far as you can go as you breathe out and hold the contraction for a second.
Pause momentarily and then breathe in as you relax your shoulders back down.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Shrug Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders, with back assisting.
instructions: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand.
Your palms should be facing your torso, with your arms extended to your sides.
Lift the dumbbells by elevating the shoulders as high as possible while you exhale.
Bring the dumbbells back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Shrug Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Shrug
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the shoulders, with back assisting.
instructions: Grasp a cable bar attachment that is fastened to a low pulley.
Your hands should be shoulder width apart, or slightly wider if you wish.
Stand close to the pulley with your arms extended in front of you holding the bar.
Lift the bar by elevating the shoulders as high as you can.
Lower the bar to its original position.

media.caption: Watch Cable Shrug Video Form Guide

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Bicep Curl
exercises.description: Wrist-friendly cambered bar curl loading both the short and long heads of the biceps brachii.
instructions: Hold the EZ-bar on the angled grips with elbows tucked comfortably at your sides.
Curl the bar upward in an arc without swinging your lower back.
Squeeze the biceps at the top and lower over 2-3 seconds to full elbow extension.

media.caption: Watch EZ-Bar Bicep Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Places the shoulder in extension to maximally stretch and recruit the long head of the biceps.
instructions: Sit back on a 45-60 degree incline bench and let your arms hang straight down behind your torso.
Keep your upper arms stationary as you curl the dumbbells with supinated wrists.
Lower all the way down until you feel a deep stretch in the biceps.

media.caption: Watch Incline Dumbbell Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Neutral-grip curl targeting the brachialis, brachioradialis, and biceps for thicker arms and forearms.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with a neutral (palms facing each other) grip.
Curl the weights up while keeping your palms neutral and elbows pinned.
Lower under control to full extension.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Hammer Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a barbell in a shoulder-width grip.
The palm of your hands should be facing forward and the elbows should be close to the torso.
Contract your biceps to curl the weight forward.
Your upper arms should remain stationary during this process.
Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder level.
Hold the contracted position for a second and squeeze the biceps hard.
Slowly bring the barbell back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Holding a dumbbell in each hand, sit on a flat bench and extend your arms down by your sides, palms facing each other.
While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the weights and start twisting the wrists once the dumbbells pass your thighs so that the palms of your hands face forward at the end of the movement.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to the starting position as your breathe in and as you rotate the wrists back to a neutral grip.

media.caption: Watch Seated Dumbbell Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Cable Curl
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a cable curl bar that is attached to a low pulley.
Grasp the bar with hands shoulder width apart and palms facing up, keeping your elbows close to your sides.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out.
Continue until your biceps are fully contracted.
Hold for a moment and then inhale as you slowly lower the bar back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Standing Cable Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Preacher Curl
exercises.description: EZ-bar exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Grab an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
Position hands at the first grip portion from the center.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length.
Begin exercise by lowering the bar down without moving your upper arms, only allowing your forearms to move.
Let forearms go all the way down until it is straight with upper arm.
Curl weight back up to starting position.

media.caption: Watch EZ-Bar Preacher Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Machine Preacher Curl
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Sit down on the Preacher Curl Machine and select the weight.
Position your triceps on the preacher pad and grasp the handles with an underhand grip.
This is the starting position.
Now lift the handles as you exhale and you contract the biceps.
At the top of the position make sure that you hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the handles back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Machine Preacher Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Curl
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Stand in the middle of two high pulleys and grasp a handle with each hand.
Your upper arms should be positioned so that they are parallel to the floor with the palms of your hands facing you.
This is the starting position for the exercise.
Slowly squeeze the biceps on each side until your forearms and biceps touch exhaling while you do so.
Slowly bring your arms back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Overhead Cable Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Rope Tricep Pushdown
exercises.description: Joint-friendly elbow extension emphasizing the lateral and medial heads of the triceps.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley and pin your elbows to your ribs.
Extend your forearms downward, spreading the rope ends apart at full lockout.
Control the return until your forearms are just above parallel.

media.caption: Watch Cable Rope Tricep Pushdown Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
exercises.description: Trains the triceps in shoulder flexion to maximally stretch and stimulate the long head.
instructions: Face away from a hip-to-shoulder height pulley holding a rope overhead.
Keep your elbows pointed forward and extend your arms overhead to lockout.
Allow a deep stretch behind your head on every eccentric.

media.caption: Watch Overhead Cable Tricep Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the triceps, with chest, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench.
Using a close grip (around shoulder width) lift the bar off the rack and hold it straight over you, keeping your arms locked.
Lower the bar to the sternum by flexing the elbows.
Maintain control and do not bounce the bar off of your chest.
After touching your torso with the bar, extend the elbows to return the bar to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Close-Grip Bench Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the triceps, with shoulders assisting.
instructions: Lie down on a flat bench holding two dumbbells directly above your shoulders.
Your arms should be fully extended and form a 90 degree angle from your torso and the floor.
Your palms should be facing in and your elbows should be tucked in close to your body.
This is your starting position.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until they are positioned near your ears.
Inhale as you do so, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Use your triceps to bring the weight up to the starting position.
Exhale as you perform this part of the exercise.

media.caption: Watch Lying Dumbbell Triceps Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Overhead Dumbbell Extension
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the triceps.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support.
Grip a dumbbell at one end using both hands.
Your palms should be facing inward.
Hold the dumbbell overhead with your arms fully extended.
This is the start position.
Keep your upper arms close to your head (biceps roughly level with your temples) and near to 90degrees to the floor.
Moving only your forearms, lower the dumbbell in a smooth arc behind your head until your forearms and biceps touch.
Hold for a count of one.

media.caption: Watch Seated Overhead Dumbbell Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Extension
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the triceps.
instructions: Sit down on a bench with your back upright, feet planted on the ground and a dumbbell in one hand.
Raise the dumbbell up until you armi is fully extended.
Lower the dumbbell to the back of your head.
tags: seated single arm overhead dumbbell tricep extensions

media.caption: Watch Single-Arm Overhead Dumbbell Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Triceps Kickback
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the triceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Brace one knee and one hand on a flat bench while keeping the other leg flat on the floor.
Your back should be flat and your torso should be parallel with the bench.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand with your palm facing inward.
Your arm should be bent at a 90 degree angle so that the dumbbell is next to your waist and your upper arm is parallel with the floor.
This is your starting position.
Without moving your upper arm, exhale and extend your arm completely back so that your entire arm is parallel with the floor and the dumbbell is perpendicular to the floor.
Hold for a moment and then slowly reverse the motion back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Triceps Kickback Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Triceps Dip
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the triceps, with chest, forearms assisting.
instructions: Place your hands on the dip bars and face your body out.
Bend at the elbows and lower your body down till your arms make a 90 degree angle.
Push yourself back up and then bring your knees up to your waist.
Lower them back down.
This completes one repetition.

media.caption: Watch Triceps Dip Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Bench Dip
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the triceps, with chest, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Balance yourself between two flat benches so that your arms are behind your back on one bench and your ankles are crossed in front of you on the other one.
For the starting position, your arms should be fully extended so that your legs are parallel with the floor.
The top half of your body should form a 90 degree angle with your legs.
Have a partner place a weight plate on your lap.
Slowly lower your body as you inhale by bending at the elbows until you lower yourself far enough to where there is an angle slightly smaller than 90 degrees between the upper arm and the forearm.
Exhale as you raise your body back up to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Bench Dip Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Single-Arm Reverse-Grip Pushdown
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the triceps.
instructions: Firmly grasp the handle, palm of your hand turning upward.
Keep your elbow tight to your body and push down till your elbow is fully stretched.
Slowly return to initial position and repeat.

media.caption: Watch Single-Arm Reverse-Grip Pushdown Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Forearm Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Direct wrist flexion movement for forearm flexor hypertrophy and grip endurance.
instructions: Rest your forearms on your thighs or a flat bench with wrists hanging over the edge, palms up.
Let the bar roll down toward your fingers, then curl your wrists upward as high as possible.
tags: palms-up barbell wrist curl over a bench

media.caption: Watch Seated Forearm Wrist Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.description: King of lower-body compound lifts developing quadriceps, glutes, adductors, and core bracing.
instructions: Position the barbell across your upper traps, unrack, and take 2-3 controlled steps back.
Take a 360-degree diaphragmatic breath, brace your core, and sit down between your hips and knees.
Descend until your hip crease passes below parallel, then drive evenly through mid-foot to stand.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Back Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: 45-Degree Leg Press
exercises.description: High-load lower-body compound movement that removes spinal loading to isolate quad and glute drive.
instructions: Sit firmly in the seat with your lower back and glutes pressed into the pad at all times.
Place feet hip-width apart on the sled, unlock the safeties, and lower until knees reach ~90 degrees or deeper without butt-wink.
Press the sled back up without hard-locking your knees.

media.caption: Watch 45-Degree Leg Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: Single-leg squat variation building unilateral quad and glute strength while eliminating side-to-side imbalances.
instructions: Elevate your rear foot laces-down on a bench behind you and hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your back knee toward the floor while keeping most of the weight on your front leg.
Drive through your front mid-foot to return to the top.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Leg Extension
exercises.description: Direct knee-extension isolation exercise uniquely training the rectus femoris alongside the vasti muscles.
instructions: Align the machine pivot point with your knee joint and position the ankle pad just above your feet.
Extend your legs fully, hold the peak quad contraction for 1 second, and lower slowly.

media.caption: Watch Seated Leg Extension Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the quads, with core, calves assisting.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip width apart.
Your toes should be pointing straight ahead or only slightly outward.
Cross your arms in front of your body, place your hands behind your head (prisoner squat) or at the sides of your head.
Keep your weight on your heels and bend your knees while lowering your hips towards the ground as if you are sitting down on a chair.
Keep your back straight at all times.
Continue until you feel a slight stretch in your quadriceps.
Pause for a count of one.
Do not let your knees extend out beyond the level of your toes.

media.caption: Watch Bodyweight Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lunge
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the quads, with core, calves assisting.
instructions: Grab a dumbbell in each hand and hold them at side of body with arms straight.
Step forward with your right leg around 2 feet or so from the foot being left stationary behind and lower your upper body down.
Step back to return to starting position.

media.caption: Watch Dumbbell Lunge Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Lunge
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the quads, with core, calves assisting.
instructions: Stand in an upright position with feet shoulder width apart and a barbell across the top of your shoulders and your hands on each side of the bar with palms facing forward.
Step forward with your right leg and squat down through your hips, while keeping the torso upright and maintaining balance.
Take a step backwards to return to starting position and then repeat the movement with the opposite leg.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Lunge Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the quads, with core, calves assisting.
instructions: Stand up straight and hold a light dumbbell close to your chest.
This is the starting position.
Squat down until your hamstrings are on your calves.
Once you get to the bottom of the squat, pause and use your elbows to push your knees out.
Return to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Goblet Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.description: Smith machine exercise for the quads, with calves assisting.
instructions: Stand with your feet turned slightly outwards, bar resting on your shoulders.
Bend your knees to about 90 degrees and push back upwards.
Keep your back straight and look straight ahead during the entire exercise.

media.caption: Watch Smith Machine Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.description: Hip-hinge powerhouse loading the hamstrings and glutes under a deep eccentric stretch.
instructions: Unrack the barbell at hip height, unlock your knees (~15 degrees), and keep the bar in contact with your thighs.
Push your hips straight back until the bar reaches mid-shin and your hamstrings are maximally stretched.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall without hyperextending your lumbar spine.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.description: Trains knee flexion with the hips flexed, placing the biarticular hamstrings in an optimal lengthened position.
instructions: Lock the thigh pad firmly over your quads so your pelvis cannot lift.
Curl your heels back underneath the seat, pause briefly, and control the eccentric.

media.caption: Watch Seated Leg Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curls
exercises.description: Prone machine hamstring curl isolating the biceps femoris, semitendinosus, and semimembranosus with hips extended.
instructions: Lie face down on the leg curl bench with the roller pad resting just above your heels and knees aligned with the pivot.
Brace your hips into the pad and curl your lower legs up until the pad reaches your glutes/upper hamstrings.
Hold peak contraction for 1 second, then lower under control over 2-3 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Lying Leg Curls Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Leg Curl
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the hamstrings, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Place yourself on a leg curl machine so that your knees are against the knee pads and your chest is against the chest pad.Place the back of your right leg underneath the curl pad so your calf is pressing against it and your toes are extended straight.
Curl your right leg up as far as possible without lifting the upper leg from the pad.
Hold for a moment and then bring the legs back to the initial position.

media.caption: Watch Standing Leg Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Targeted horizontal hip extension maximizing gluteus maximus tension at full hip lockout.
instructions: Rest your upper back (just below the scapulae) against a sturdy bench with a padded barbell over your hips.
Tuck your chin, keep ribs down, and drive through your heels until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the glute squeeze for 1-2 seconds at the top.

media.caption: Watch Barbell Hip Thrust Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Hüftabduktion / Hip Adduction
exercises.description: Seated machine hip abduction and adduction strengthening the gluteus medius/minimus and inner thigh adductors for pelvic stability.
instructions: Sit tall in the machine with your back against the pad and position the knee pads comfortably.
Drive your knees outward (abduction) or squeeze inward (adduction) smoothly through a full range of motion.
Pause 1 second at peak contraction and control the eccentric without letting the weight stack slam.

media.caption: Watch Hüftabduktion / Hip Adduction Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the glutes, with core, back assisting.
instructions: Lie flat on the floor on your back with the hands by your side and your knees bent.
Your feet should be placed around shoulder width.
Begin exercise by squeezing your glutes and raising hips up until your body forms a straight line from your knees to your shoulders.
Hold for at least 5 seconds, then lower back down.

media.caption: Watch Glute Bridge Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Weighted Glute Bridge
exercises.description: Barbell exercise for the glutes, with core, hamstrings assisting.
instructions: Lie down with back on an exercise mat and arms straight at your sides.
Place a weight plate on your hips and hold in place with your hands.
Begin the movement by driving through with your heels, extending your hips vertically through the bar.
Extend as far as possible, then reverse the motion to return to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Weighted Glute Bridge Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.description: Straight-knee ankle plantarflexion emphasizing the gastrocnemius and soleus across a full stretch.
instructions: Place the balls of your feet on the platform with knees straight (not hyperextended).
Lower your heels into a 2-second bottom stretch, then press up tall onto the balls of your feet.

media.caption: Watch Standing Calf Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: Bent-knee plantarflexion isolating the soleus muscle underneath the gastrocnemius for complete lower-leg development.
instructions: Sit on the machine with the balls of your feet on the step and the thigh pad snug just above your knees.
Lower your heels as far as ankle mobility allows for a 2-second stretch, then drive up to full contraction.

media.caption: Watch Seated Calf Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.description: Dynamic spinal flexion and hip flexion movement building the rectus abdominis and hip flexors.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an active shoulder pack.
Curl your pelvis upward toward your ribs as you raise your legs, avoiding momentum.
Lower slowly to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Hanging Leg Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
exercises.description: Weighted spinal flexion allowing progressive overload of the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Kneel below a high pulley holding a rope attachment beside your temples.
Flex your spine by curling your sternum toward your pelvis while keeping your hips stationary.

media.caption: Watch Kneeling Cable Crunch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Psoas / Hip Flexor March
exercises.description: Direct hip-flexion strengthening for the iliopsoas and rectus femoris to improve sprint mechanics and hip stability.
instructions: Loop a mini-band or light kettlebell around your feet while standing tall next to a rack.
Drive one knee above 90 degrees of hip flexion, hold for 2 seconds with a tall posture, and lower.

media.caption: Watch Standing Psoas / Hip Flexor March Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: Total-body posterior chain pull recruiting glutes, hamstrings, spinal erectors, traps, lats, and grip.
instructions: Stand with mid-foot under the barbell, grip just outside your shins, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Brace your lats and core, push the floor away with your legs, and lock out hips and knees simultaneously.

media.caption: Watch Conventional Barbell Deadlift Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Rowing Ergometer (Concept2)
exercises.description: Low-impact full-body cardiovascular conditioning engaging legs, core, and upper back.
instructions: Drive with the legs first, swing the torso back slightly, and finish by pulling the handle to your lower ribs.
Recover in reverse order: arms away, torso hinge forward, then bend the knees.

media.caption: Watch Rowing Ergometer (Concept2) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie down on the floor on your back and bend your knees, placing your hands behind your head or across your chest.
Brace your core.
Crunch your ribs toward your pelvis using your abdominal muscles to initiate and complete the movement.
Exhale as you come up and keep your neck straight, chin up.
Hold at the top of the movement for a few seconds, breathing continuously.
Lower slowly back down.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Crunch
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of the decline bench and lie down.
Place hands behind head or cross arms over chest.
Begin exercise by raising torso to a sitting position, pause, then lower back down.

media.caption: Watch Decline Bench Crunch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Ab Crunch Machine
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the core.
instructions: Select an appropriate resistance and sit down on the ab machine placing your feet under the pads provided and grabbing the top handles.
Your arms should be bent at a 90 degree angle as you rest the triceps on the pads provided.
This will be your starting position.
Next, tighten the abdominals and while breathing out, crunch your abs.
To do this, bend at the waist, lowering the hand bars and lifting the legs.
Breathing in, straighten your torso without letting the weight plates hit.
Pause briefly and then repeat.

media.caption: Watch Ab Crunch Machine Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternate Heel Touchers
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie on the floor or an exercise mat with the knees bent and the feet on the floor around 18-24 inches apart.
Breathing out, crunch your ab slightly upward and sideways to the right a couple of inches until your right hand touches your right heel.
Now go back slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat on the other side.

media.caption: Watch Alternate Heel Touchers Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Lie facedown on a flat bench with the hips on the edge of the bench and the legs straight.
Start the movement by lifting the left leg higher than the right leg.
Then lower the left leg as you lift the right leg.
Continue alternating.

media.caption: Watch Flutter Kicks Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Elbow-to-Knee Crunch
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes, quads assisting.
instructions: Crunch your left knee, while bending it, and right elbow so that they meet at the center of your body.
Return to starting position and crunch your right knee to your left elbow.

media.caption: Watch Elbow-to-Knee Crunch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Get down on your hands and knees with your arms shoulder-width apart and hands directly underneath your shoulders.
Begin the exercise by simultaneously raising your right arm up and your left leg up at the same time until they are both in line with the rest of your body.
Hold this position for a brief moment and then return to starting position.
Repeat with opposite leg and arm.

media.caption: Watch Bird Dog Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cable Core Rotation
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the core.
instructions: Hold a cable with both hands to your right side, so your left arm is straight and stretched across your body.
Pull the cable to the opposite side rotating your torso until your right arm is straight.
Return the cable back to starting position and repeat.

media.caption: Watch Cable Core Rotation Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
exercises.description: Machine exercise for the core, with back assisting.
instructions: Place your forearms are on the pads or bars of the apparatus you are using and grip the handles or bars.
Your arms should be bent at 90 degrees and your upper arms in a straight line with your sides.
Your torso should be straight and your lower back pressed against the pad of the bench if using one.
Keep your legs extended and pointing down to the floor.
This is the start position.
Exhale and as you do so, lift your legs up in a smooth arc bending at the knees until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Hold for a count of one.
Return to the start position in a smooth, controlled movement while inhaling.
tags: captain's chair leg / knee / hip raise

media.caption: Watch Captain's Chair Knee Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie on your right side, legs extended and stacked from hip to feet.
The elbow of your right arm is directly under your shoulder.
Ensure your head is directly in line with your spine.
Your left arm can be aligned along the left side of your body.
Engage your abdominal muscles, drawing your navel toward your spine.
Lift your hips and knees from the mat while exhaling.
Your torso is straight in line with no sagging or bending.
Hold the position.

media.caption: Watch Side Plank Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Side Jackknife
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Lie on your left side, your legs stacked and straight.
Wrap your left arm in front of your torso, placing it on your right hip, and put your right hand behind your head.
Simultaneously raise your torso and legs, bringing your head toward your hips.
Return to start in a controlled motion.

media.caption: Watch Side Jackknife Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Jackknife Sit-Up
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Lie on your back on an exercise mat on the floor with your legs touching and fully extended and your arms extended outward with palms down.
As you exhale, bend at the waist while simultaneously raising your legs and arms to meet in a jackknife position.
While inhaling, lower your arms and legs back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Jackknife Sit-Up Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Leg Pull-In
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with back assisting.
instructions: Lie on an exercise mat with your legs extended and your hands either palms facing down next to you or under your glutes.
Bend your knees and raise your legs so that they form a 90 degree angle.
Begin exercise by extending your legs out and touching the floor with your toes so that you feel a tight stretch in your lower abs.
Return to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Leg Pull-In Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with back assisting.
instructions: Lay down with your back flat on the floor, feet straight out and together and your hands on your side.
While keep your legs as straight as you can lift your feet up in the air between 6-12 inches.
You can either hold for designated period of time or you can raise them up and then lower them right back down.

media.caption: Watch Lying Leg Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with glutes assisting.
instructions: Lie face up on a falt bench.
Place hands behind head and raise head off the ground.
Next, lift your legs and bend knees so that they form a 90-degree angle.
Hips are still on the ground at this time.
Begin exercise by raising your hips off the ground and toward your head.
Pause for a moment, then lower back down and repeat.

media.caption: Watch Reverse Crunch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Exercise Ball Crunch
exercises.description: Equipment-based exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie on an exercise ball with your lower back pressed against the surface of the ball.
Your legs should be bent at the knee, your feet should be flat on the floor.
When you are in the proper position, your upper torso should be hanging off the top of the ball.
Keep your arms at your sides or crossed on top of your chest.
Lower your torso into a stretch position keeping the neck stationary at all times.
This will be your starting position.
With your hips stationary, contract your abs to flex your waist.
Curl your shoulders and trunk up until you feel a contraction in your abs.

media.caption: Watch Exercise Ball Crunch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Couch Stretch (Hip Flexor & Quad)
exercises.description: Deep time-based stretch opening the iliopsoas and rectus femoris after sitting or heavy lower-body training.
instructions: Place your rear knee at the base of a wall or bench with your shin vertical against the surface.
Step your front foot into a lunge, posteriorly tilt your pelvis (squeeze the rear glute), and breathe deeply.
Hold for 45-60 seconds per side.

media.caption: Watch Couch Stretch (Hip Flexor & Quad) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Internal & External Rotation
exercises.description: Active mobility flow improving hip capsule internal and external rotation for deeper, pain-free squats.
instructions: Sit on the floor with both front and back knees bent at 90-degree angles.
Hinge forward over your front shin with a flat back, then rotate smoothly to the opposite 90/90 position.

media.caption: Watch 90/90 Hip Internal & External Rotation Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Open Book & Pec Stretch
exercises.description: Restores thoracic rotation and opens tight pectorals and anterior shoulders before or after pressing.
instructions: Lie on your side with top knee bent at 90 degrees resting on the floor or a foam roller.
Sweep your top arm in an arc across your body toward the floor behind you while exhaling slowly.

media.caption: Watch Thoracic Spine Open Book & Pec Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Doorway Pec Major & Minor Stretch
exercises.description: Static stretch releasing tight chest and anterior deltoid fascia.
instructions: Place your forearms against a doorway or power rack upright with elbows at 90-110 degrees.
Step gently through the frame until a comfortable stretch is felt across the chest, holding for 45 seconds.
tags: chest and front of shoulder stretch

media.caption: Watch Doorway Pec Major & Minor Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Supine Banded Hamstring & Calf Stretch
exercises.description: Decompressed posterior-chain stretch targeting the hamstrings and gastrocnemius without lumbar strain.
instructions: Lie on your back, loop a band around one foot, and extend the leg ceiling-ward.
Contract and relax the quad for 5-second PNF cycles over 60 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Supine Banded Hamstring & Calf Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Pigeon / Figure-4 Piriformis & Glute Stretch
exercises.description: Deep external-rotation hip stretch releasing the gluteus medius, piriformis, and deep lateral hip rotators to relieve lower-back tightness.
instructions: Cross one shin in front of your hips (or ankle over opposite knee if lying on your back).
Keep your pelvis squared and hinge forward gently from the hips while exhaling slowly.
Hold for 45-60 seconds per side without forcing knee torque.

media.caption: Watch Pigeon / Figure-4 Piriformis & Glute Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch (Lunge & T-Spine Reach)
exercises.description: Multi-planar dynamic warm-up flow simultaneously opening hip flexors, adductors, hamstrings, and thoracic rotation.
instructions: Step into a deep forward lunge and plant your opposite hand on the floor inside your front foot.
Drop your inside elbow toward your front instep, then rotate your torso and reach that arm toward the ceiling.
Shift your hips back briefly to lengthen the front hamstring before switching sides.

media.caption: Watch World's Greatest Stretch (Lunge & T-Spine Reach) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Butterfly Groin & Adductor Stretch
exercises.description: Opens the inner-thigh adductors and pelvic floor for wider, more comfortable squat and sumo stances.
instructions: Sit tall on the floor, bring the soles of your feet together, and hold your ankles.
Use your elbows to gently press your knees toward the floor while maintaining a neutral spine.
Breathe deeply into your pelvis for 45-60 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Seated Butterfly Groin & Adductor Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold & Ankle Dorsiflexion Pry
exercises.description: Loaded ankle dorsiflexion and hip-opening mobility drill essential for upright squat mechanics and knee tracking.
instructions: Sink into the bottom of a deep bodyweight squat with heels flat on the floor (hold a rack upright if needed).
Place your elbows inside your knees and gently shift weight side-to-side over each ankle to mobilize the talocrural joint.
Accumulate 60 seconds with an upright chest.

media.caption: Watch Deep Squat Hold & Ankle Dorsiflexion Pry Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing Wall Gastrocnemius & Soleus Stretch
exercises.description: Dual-position ankle dorsiflexion stretch releasing both straight-knee gastrocnemius and bent-knee soleus/Achilles tension.
instructions: Place hands on a wall and step one foot back with heel pressed firmly into the floor and knee straight for 30 seconds.
Slightly bend the rear knee while keeping the heel down for another 30 seconds to target the soleus and Achilles tendon.

media.caption: Watch Standing Wall Gastrocnemius & Soleus Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Standing / Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch
exercises.description: Lengthens the rectus femoris and vasti muscles while encouraging posterior pelvic tilt.
instructions: Stand on one leg (holding a rack for balance), grab your opposite ankle, and pull your heel toward your glute.
Keep both knees close together and lightly squeeze your glute to prevent lower-back overarching.

media.caption: Watch Standing / Side-Lying Quadriceps Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Seated Floor Hamstring & Posterior Chain Fold
exercises.description: Static floor stretch lengthening the hamstrings, calves, and thoracolumbar fascia without equipment.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs extended straight in front of you and toes dorsiflexed.
Hinge forward from the hip crease keeping your chest long, reaching toward your shins or feet for 45-60 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Seated Floor Hamstring & Posterior Chain Fold Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Child's Pose & Side-Reach Lat Decompression
exercises.description: Opens the latissimus dorsi, teres major, and thoracic spine while gently decompressing the lumbar vertebrae.
instructions: Kneel on the floor, sit your hips back onto your heels, and reach your arms long in front of you.
Walk both hands 30 degrees to the left to bias the right lat for 30 seconds, then walk hands to the right for 30 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Child's Pose & Side-Reach Lat Decompression Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cross-Body Posterior Deltoid & Capsule Stretch
exercises.description: Releases posterior shoulder capsule and rear deltoid tightness after pressing or upper-back sessions.
instructions: Bring one arm straight across your chest at shoulder height while keeping your shoulder blade depressed.
Use your opposite forearm to gently draw the arm closer to your chest for 45 seconds per side.

media.caption: Watch Cross-Body Posterior Deltoid & Capsule Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Overhead Triceps & Lateral Fascia Stretch
exercises.description: Targets the long head of the triceps brachii and upper latissimus dorsi in full shoulder flexion.
instructions: Reach one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand touches your upper back between the shoulder blades.
Gently press the elbow back and slightly side-bend away for 45 seconds per arm.

media.caption: Watch Overhead Triceps & Lateral Fascia Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Passive Bar Hang (Shoulder & Spinal Decompression)
exercises.description: Traction hang opening the subacromial shoulder space, stretching the lats and pecs, and decompressing intervertebral discs.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip and let your body hang with relaxed hips and legs.
Allow your shoulders to elevate gently toward your ears while taking slow 4-second nasal breaths for 45-60 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Passive Bar Hang (Shoulder & Spinal Decompression) Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Kneeling Wrist Flexor & Extensor Mobility
exercises.description: Restores wrist extension and forearm flexor elasticity for pain-free bench pressing, push-ups, and front squats.
instructions: Kneel on all fours and place your palms flat on the floor with fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Slowly rock your hips backward a few inches until a steady stretch is felt along the inner forearms for 45 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Kneeling Wrist Flexor & Extensor Mobility Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Segmental Spinal Articulation
exercises.description: Rhythmic flexion and extension flow lubricating the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar facet joints.
instructions: Start in a quadruped position with hands stacked under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale as you drop your belly and lift your sternum (Cow), then exhale as you press the floor away and round your spine (Cat).
Flow smoothly for 10-12 breath cycles (~60 seconds).

media.caption: Watch Cat-Cow Segmental Spinal Articulation Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Supine Knee-to-Chest & Lumbar Decompression
exercises.description: Gentle floor decompression releasing the lumbar erectors, sacroiliac joint, and gluteus maximus after heavy squats or deadlifts.
instructions: Lie flat on your back and draw both knees (or one knee at a time) gently into your chest.
Rock slowly side-to-side across your sacrum while taking deep diaphragmatic breaths for 60 seconds.

media.caption: Watch Supine Knee-to-Chest & Lumbar Decompression Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Lateral Neck & Upper Trapezius Release
exercises.description: Relieves cervical tension, upper trapezius hypertonicity, and levator scapulae stiffness from desk work or heavy shrugs.
instructions: Sit or stand tall, anchor one hand behind your lower back to depress the shoulder.
Gently tilt your ear toward the opposite shoulder until a mild stretch is felt along the side of the neck for 45 seconds per side.

media.caption: Watch Lateral Neck & Upper Trapezius Release Video Form Guide

exercises.name: 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Begin in a half kneeling position with the
leg away from the wall stabilized against the wall
with a ball.
With both hands directly in front of
you, rotate one arm open attempting to reach
the wall behind you.
Exhale as you rotate, inhale
as you return to neutral and repeat.

media.caption: Watch 1/2 Kneeling Thoracic Rotation Video Form Guide

exercises.name: 1 Leg Box Squat
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the hamstrings, with quadriceps assisting.
instructions: This exercise requires a sturdy box or a chair. Simple stand ~6 inches in front of it and balance yourself on one leg. From here, begin squatting down in a smooth controlled motion while keeping your other leg straight out in front of you for balance. Slowly sit down on the box, pause for a 1 count and push back up with the working leg, while never letting your other leg touch the ground.

media.caption: Watch 1 Leg Box Squat Video Form Guide

exercises.name: 3/4 Sit-Up
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

exercises.name: 4-count burpees
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the chest.
instructions: Starting position:
Stand straight, feet hip-width apart.
Steps:
Squat low and support yourself on the floor with your hands between the knees and in front of your feet, your back straight.
Keeping your hands on the floor, jump your legs backward into high plank position.
Jump your feet forward to return to the squat position.
Repeat.

exercises.name: Ab Roller
exercises.description: Accessory exercise for the core, with shoulders assisting.
instructions: Hold the Ab Roller with both hands and kneel on the floor.
Now place the ab roller on the floor in front of you so that you are on all your hands and knees (as in a kneeling push up position). This will be your starting position.

Slowly roll the ab roller straight forward, stretching your body into a straight position. Tip: Go down as far as you can without touching the floor with your body. Breathe in during this portion of the movement.
After a pause at the stretched position, start pulling yourself back to the starting position as you breathe out. Tip: Go slowly and keep your abs tight at all times.

media.caption: Watch Ab Roller Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Ab wheel
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core, with chest assisting.
instructions: Starting Position: Kneel on the floor with the ab wheel in front of you.
Grip the Wheel: Hold the handles firmly.
Roll Out: Slowly roll the wheel forward, extending your body while keeping your core tight.
Return: Pull the wheel back towards your knees, maintaining tension in your core.

media.caption: Watch Ab wheel Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Abdominal Draw-In
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie
on your back with knees bent. Gently pull your belly button toward your
spine without moving your hips or holding your breath.

media.caption: Watch Abdominal Draw-In Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Abduction while standing
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the quadriceps.
instructions: Training a stable stance, predominantly on one leg, is crucial for both sides. On the one hand, it prevents discomfort and, on the other, it establishes a stable foundation. The practitioner assumes the usual standing position and, with a stable upper body, attempts to repeatedly lift the unloaded leg, bend it at the hip and knee, and then lower it again. The movement is also repeated on the other side. The exercise trains the stability of the hip-surrounding muscles.

media.caption: Watch Abduction while standing Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Adductor
exercises.description: Foam roller exercise for the quadriceps.
instructions: Lie face down with one leg on a foam roll.
Rotate the leg so that the foam roll contacts against your inner thigh. Shift as much weight onto the foam roll as can be tolerated.
While trying to relax the muscles if the inner thigh, roll over the foam between your hip and knee, holding points of tension for 10-30 seconds. Repeat with the other leg.

exercises.name: Adductor/Groin
exercises.description: Equipment-free exercise for the quadriceps.
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet raised towards the ceiling.
Have your partner hold your feet or ankles. Abduct your legs as far as you can. This will be your starting position.
Attempt to squeeze your legs together for 10 or more seconds, while your partner prevents you from doing so.

Now, relax the muscles in your legs as your partner pushes your feet apart, stretching as far as is comfortable for you. Be sure to let your partner know when the stretch is adequate to prevent overstretching or injury.

exercises.name: Advanced Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the core, with glutes, hamstrings, shoulders assisting.
instructions: Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with one arm.

Keeping the kettlebell locked out at all times, push your butt out in the direction of the locked out kettlebell. Keep the non-working arm behind your back and turn your feet out at a forty-five degree angle from the arm with the kettlebell.
Lower yourself as far as possible.
Pause for a second and reverse the motion back to the starting position.

media.caption: Watch Advanced Kettlebell Windmill Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Air Bike
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the core.
instructions: Lie flat on the floor with your lower back pressed to the ground. For this exercise, you will need to put your hands beside your head. Be careful however to not strain with the neck as you perform it. Now lift your shoulders into the crunch position.
Bring knees up to where they are perpendicular to the floor, with your lower legs parallel to the floor. This will be your starting position.

Now simultaneously, slowly go through a cycle pedal motion kicking forward with the right leg and bringing in the knee of the left leg. Bring your right elbow close to your left knee by crunching to the side, as you breathe out.
Go back to the initial position as you breathe in.
Crunch to the opposite side as you cycle your legs and bring closer your left elbow to your right knee and exhale.
Continue alternating in this manner until all of the recommended repetitions for each side have been completed.

media.caption: Watch Air Bike Video Form Guide

exercises.name: All Fours Quad Stretch
exercises.description: Bodyweight exercise for the quadriceps.
instructions: Start off on your hands and knees, then lift your leg off the floor and hold the foot with your hand.
Use your hand to hold the foot or ankle, keeping the knee fully flexed, stretching the quadriceps and hip flexors.
Focus on extending your hips, thrusting them towards the floor. Hold for 10-20 seconds and then switch sides.

media.caption: Watch All Fours Quad Stretch Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternate Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright and a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. The elbows should be close to the torso.
The palms of the hands should be facing your torso. This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbells back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

media.caption: Watch Alternate Hammer Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the biceps, with forearms assisting.
instructions: Sit down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand being held at arms length. Tip: Keep the elbows close to the torso.This will be your starting position.

While holding the upper arm stationary, curl the right weight forward while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. As you do so, rotate the hand so that the palm is facing up. Continue the movement until your biceps is fully contracted and the dumbbells are at shoulder level. Hold the contracted position for a second as you squeeze the biceps. Tip: Only the forearms should move.
Slowly begin to bring the dumbbell back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat the movement with the left hand. This equals one repetition.
Continue alternating in this manner for the recommended amount of repetitions.

media.caption: Watch Alternate Incline Dumbbell Curl Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
exercises.description: Equipment-free exercise for the quadriceps, with glutes, calves, hamstrings assisting.
instructions: Assume a comfortable stance with one foot slightly in front of the other.
Begin by pushing off with the front leg, driving the opposite knee forward and as high as possible before landing. Attempt to cover as much distance to each side with each bound.
It may help to use a line on the ground to guage distance from side to side.
Repeat the sequence with the other leg.

media.caption: Watch Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating bicep curls
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Starting position:

Start standing up with dumbbells in each hand, your back straight and feet hip-width apart. Your arms should be relaxed, pointing down. Your knees should be slightly bent, your abs contracted, and your shoulders down.
Steps:
Bend one arm at the elbow, bringing the dumbbell up to your shoulder. Your upper arm should remain motionless during this movement.
Bring the dumbbell back down until your arm is in its original relaxed position.
Repeat, switching arms.

media.caption: Watch Alternating bicep curls Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Cable Shoulder Press
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the shoulders, with triceps assisting.
instructions: Move the cables to the bottom of the tower and select an appropriate weight.
Grasp the cables and hold them at shoulder height, palms facing forward. This will be your starting position.
Keeping your head and chest up, extend through the elbow to press one side directly over head.
After pausing at the top, return to the starting position and repeat on the opposite side.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Cable Shoulder Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
exercises.description: Dumbbell exercise for the shoulders.
instructions: In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side.
Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
Return the weights to your side.
On the next repetition, raise the weights laterally, raising them out to your side to about shoulder height.
Return the weights to the starting position and continue alternating to the front and side.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Deltoid Raise Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Floor Press
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the chest, with core, shoulders, triceps assisting.
instructions: Lie on the floor with two kettlebells next to your shoulders.
Position one in place on your chest and then the other, gripping the kettlebells on the handle with the palms facing forward.
Extend both arms, so that the kettlebells are being held above your chest. Lower one kettlebell, bringing it to your chest and turn the wrist in the direction of the locked out kettlebell.
Raise the kettlebell and repeat on the opposite side.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Floor Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Hang Clean
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the hamstrings, with biceps, calves, forearms, glutes, back assisting.
instructions: Place two kettlebells between your feet. To get in the starting position, push your butt back and look straight ahead.

Clean one kettlebell to your shoulder and hold on to the other kettlebell in a hanging position. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebell towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrist as you do so.
Lower the cleaned kettlebell to a hanging position and clean the alternate kettlebell. Repeat.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Hang Clean Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating High Cable Row
exercises.description: Cable exercise for the back.
instructions: Start
by putting the attachment in a high position on the cable station and step back about 1m from the attachment. Grab
the cable pulley handle in your left hand at about head height with your elbow slightly bent. Step back with your left foot.
Pull
your elbow joint in toward the torso twisting slightly and perform a
single-arm row. Engage the lats as you twist.
Return
to the starting position with cable pulley and left foot and grab the cable pulley handle in the right

media.caption: Watch Alternating High Cable Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Kettlebell Press
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the shoulders, with triceps assisting.
instructions: Clean two kettlebells to your shoulders. Clean the kettlebells to your shoulders by extending through the legs and hips as you pull the kettlebells towards your shoulders. Rotate your wrists as you do so.
Press one directly overhead by extending through the elbow, turning it so the palm faces forward while holding the other kettlebell stationary .
Lower the pressed kettlebell to the starting position and immediately press with your other arm.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Kettlebell Press Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Kettlebell Row
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the back, with biceps assisting.
instructions: Place two kettlebells in front of your feet. Bend your knees slightly and push your butt out as much as possible. As you bend over to get into the starting position grab both kettlebells by the handles.

Pull one kettlebell off of the floor while holding on to the other kettlebell. Retract the shoulder blade of the working side, as you flex the elbow, drawing the kettlebell towards your stomach or rib cage.
Lower the kettlebell in the working arm and repeat with your other arm.

media.caption: Watch Alternating Kettlebell Row Video Form Guide

exercises.name: Alternating Renegade Row
exercises.description: Kettlebell exercise for the back, with core, biceps, chest, triceps assisting.
